first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I gave it the first screen. It is calm and it knows the difference between the Church and the family folklore. Nothing cheap, nothing gushing. But it is a guide for guests and ordinary couples, not for someone planning 300 people over several days. I read the service and reception parts, skimmed the legal section, and looked for any sign this team has done something at my scale. There isn't one.

journey.quote: It says plainly which belong to the Church and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone who separates the sacrament from the folklore understands families like mine. That is the cultural awareness I look for.

journey.quote: Customs such as the krevati, names on the shoe and koufeta are family folklore that varies by region, so ask your own family how they do it.
journey.reaction: Respectful. They don't tell my mother how her island does things. No stereotyping.

journey.quote: It is a light moment that photographs well.
journey.reaction: Everything 'photographs well' at a wedding. My question is who controls those photographs. The article never touches privacy around the getting-ready moments, and it can't, it's a general guide. Minor.

journey.quote: It is a gesture of good wishes from family, and many couples now ask a koumbaros or cousin to gather it discreetly.
journey.reaction: 'Discreetly' is the right instinct. With a few hundred guests the money dance is a security matter, not a cousin's job, but at least the tone is right.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Greece as an Australian
journey.quote: This section reflects official advice as at November 2026 and is not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Careful and dated, which I respect. But this is my lawyer's and my assistant's territory. I skimmed it.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Greece as an Australian
journey.quote: With [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge), one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the plans around the day, from [Greece wedding venues](/destinations/europe/greece) to guest travel, and the fee and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Single point of contact, yes, that is what my family office wants. 'Fee and inclusions' reads a little like a package menu though. And 'guest travel' is not the same as moving 300 people, VIPs and a security detail. Nothing here tells me they have done it at my size.

journey.quote: If you would like to talk through the plans around the day, venues, guest travel and timing, a Wedded Advisor is glad to start that conversation.
journey.reaction: Polite, not pushy. 'Glad to' is a touch eager but fine. Still, I would not enquire from a blog footer. I'd want a private introduction.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered a Greek Orthodox wedding with 200 to 400 guests, in Greece or Australia?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a venue or island property for several days?
Do they work with a family's own security team, and handle NDAs for vendors and photographers?
Can they coordinate private aviation, private transfers and VIP arrivals for guests from Dubai, London and Sydney?
Is there a private or referral channel to speak with a senior planner, rather than a general enquiry form?
Can they work with a specific parish priest or diocese in Greece on a private chapel ceremony?

turn_offs_found.quote: and the fee and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Inclusions' sounds like a package tier. I don't want to be slotted into a menu. Small, but it is the one phrase that made me feel like a standard client.

would_share_with: My assistant, to file as background for the Greek side of the family
Cousins who are guests and need to know what to wear and expect

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to talk through the plans around the day, venues, guest travel and timing, a Wedded Advisor is glad to start that conversation.
cta_reaction.why: Not because anything offended me. It is a good, tasteful guide, but it shows knowledge of the custom, not capacity for my scale or discretion. I only enquire through a referral or a private channel, and this page gives me no reason to ask my assistant to find one.

top_3_changes: Near the Wedded Concierge line, add one understated sentence (only if true and sourced) that the team handles very large guest lists, exclusive use and private transfers, so a family planning at scale sees it is possible.
Swap 'fee and inclusions' for wording that feels bespoke rather than tiered, for example that the scope and fee are agreed in writing before you commit.
Offer a quieter, private route to a senior advisor alongside the general CTA, for families who would rather be introduced than fill in a form.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, 200 to 400 guests, discretion first)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Missing business details and absence of prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: This is an informational traditions post; low relevance and enquiry intent from the UHNW persona is expected. Weigh my scores accordingly rather than as a draft failure.
Is there sourced evidence of large-scale or exclusive-use delivery that could support one understated line near the Concierge mention? If not, leave it out.
